lines.text: Inside the outlined area, all the way across from the top edge. Its bottom is about 5 in from the top edge.
Paints: Soft sky blue over nearly all of it, with Warm apricot and Golden ochre only at the right edge, low down.
Mix enough Warm apricot for this step and step 2; cover it between them.
Mix enough Golden ochre for this step and steps 3, 14, 15 and 24; cover it between them.
Brush: 1 inch flat. Load: Creamy paint. An even coat.
Start with the darkest color and stroke side to side. Without rinsing, pick up the next lighter color and paint below it. Then stroke back up over the join several times.
It should leave smooth bands of color, with a soft join where two wet colors meet.
Watch out: Blending after the paint has started to drag. Acrylic sets in minutes, and scrubbing setting paint lifts it and leaves streaks. Fix: stop as soon as it drags.
Let it dry, then blend a new thin layer on top.

lines.text: Let the sunset sky dry to the touch first. A hair dryer on low speeds it up.
Inside the outlined area, all the way across from the top edge. Its bottom is about 2 1/2 in from the top edge.
Paints, darkest first: Warm apricot, then Pale silver-gray. The paint map shows where each goes.
Mix enough Pale silver-gray for this step and step 5; cover it between them.
Brush: 1/2 inch flat. Load: Wiped nearly dry. Only the tip goes in the paint, and no water on the brush. It should feel dry and hard to apply.
Light pressure, skimming the surface.
It should leave feathery, broken, see-through marks that catch the canvas texture. Never a solid area.
Watch out: Hard, solid clouds. Too much paint on the brush. Fix: wipe the brush nearly dry and use small circles with the tip, so the sky shows through the edges.
